en: Arjuna said: Krishna, what about those who set aside the rules of scripture but worship with faith? Is their standing sattva, rajas or tamas?

first: त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा ।
en: Krishna said: The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds, born of their nature: sattvic, rajasic and tamasic. Hear about it.
The faith of each person follows their inner nature, Bharata. A person is made of faith: whatever their faith is, that is what they are.
Sattvic people worship the gods; rajasic people worship Yakshas and Rakshasas; and the others, tamasic people, worship ghosts and spirits.

first: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः ।
en: People who practise harsh austerities not taught by scripture, full of pretence and ego, driven by the force of desire and attachment,
senselessly torturing the elements in their body and me who live within the body: know that their resolve is demonic.
Even the food that people like is of three kinds, and so are sacrifice, austerity and giving. Hear how they differ.
Foods that increase life, goodness, strength, health, happiness and cheer, that are tasty, rich, nourishing and pleasing, are liked by sattvic people.
Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, sharp, dry and burning are liked by rajasic people; they bring pain, sorrow and illness.

first: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् ।
en: Food that is stale, tasteless, rotten, left overnight, left over by others and impure is liked by tamasic people.
Sacrifice offered according to the rules by those who do not want its fruit, with the mind fixed on the thought that it simply ought to be done, is sattvic.

first: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।
en: But sacrifice offered with an eye on its fruit, or for show, know it to be rajasic, best of the Bharatas.
Sacrifice without rules, without sharing food, without sacred words, without gifts to the priests and without faith is called tamasic.
Honouring the gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise, along with purity, honesty, self-restraint (brahmacharya) and non-violence, is called austerity of the body.

first: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
en: Speech that causes no distress and is true, pleasant and helpful, along with regular study of scripture, is called austerity of speech.
A clear and calm mind, gentleness, silence, self-control and purity of heart are called austerity of the mind.
This threefold austerity, practised with the highest faith by steady people who do not want its fruit, is called sattvic.
Austerity done with pretence, to gain respect, honour and praise, is called rajasic here. It is unsteady and does not last.
Austerity done out of foolish stubbornness, with torture of oneself, or to harm another, is called tamasic.
A gift given because it ought to be given, to one who cannot return the favour, at the right place and time and to a worthy person, is called sattvic.
But a gift given to get something back, or with an eye on reward, or given unwillingly, is called rajasic.
A gift given at the wrong place and time to unworthy people, without respect and with contempt, is called tamasic.
'Om Tat Sat' is said to be the threefold name of Brahman. By it, long ago, the Brahmins, the Vedas and the sacrifices were set in place.
So those who follow Brahman always begin acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity, done according to the rules, by saying 'Om'.
Saying 'Tat', those who seek freedom perform the various acts of sacrifice, austerity and giving without aiming for any fruit.
The word 'Sat' is used to mean what is real and what is good. So too, Partha, the word 'Sat' is used for a praiseworthy act.

first: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते ।
en: Steadiness in sacrifice, austerity and giving is also called 'Sat', and any action done for that purpose is also called 'Sat'.

first: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् ।
en: Whatever is offered, given, practised as austerity or done without faith is called 'asat', Partha. It is of no use here or after death.
